about: Which body each class wears, and which animation plays for what. Read by the director when a battle is built; see Docs/CharacterSetup.md. A class is looked up by its id under classes, then by its look under looks, then default. Every body names an animation set, and every animation in a set must be authored for that body's skeleton. The mannequin set has no hit clip: the template's hit reactions are additive, made to be layered over another pose, and cannot play on their own. Each set may map motions (melee, heavy, shoot, bolt, area, heal, buff, revive, channel, dash) to clips: 'release' when it goes off (one per slot, round), and for a cast 'intro' and a looping 'windup' while it charges, then 'castRelease'. A motion a set lacks falls back to a near one (heavy to melee, area to bolt, heal and buff to each other) and at last to the set's attack or cast. Sets may also name clips for reactions, statuses and moments, each a clip or a list: hitFront/hitBack/hitLeft/hitRight/hitHeavy (by where the blow came from; hitHeavy for a critical), evade, block, deathFront/deathBack/deathLeft/deathRight (the fall for a blow from that side: from the front, it goes over backwards), stunned and sleep (looped while it lasts), ready (its turn begins), victory and defeat (the battle is decided), and 'idles': {motion: clip} for a stance that suits a class whose first ability has that motion. A motion may also give 'impact': how far into its release the blow lands, 0 to 1. Clips were chosen by watching Tools\AnimCatalog.bat's film; the hit reactions both packs ship are additive and cannot be used. heroPlan names the Paragon hero each class should wear, and heroLooks the hero for each look -- either one hero or a list, best first, of which the first installed is worn; Tools/assign_bodies.py turns them into classes and looks for the heroes that are installed, giving classes on the same hero different skins (a skin is a body '<hero>_<skin>' sharing the hero's animations). bodyScale sizes a body, or every body of an animation set (a hero and its skins): Sevarog and GRIM are built three metres tall.
